text:
olivia (eng-platform): FYI canary 2026-06-05 02:40 UTC is showing elevated 5xx for model-v3-small, +30% error rate vs baseline. Rolling back?

mike (eng-runtime): saw that too. latency looks fine but there are a handful of kv-miss spikes around prefix cache. suspect interaction with new session-affinity change.

sara (eng-sre): @mike what region? is it global or just us-east-1?

mike (eng-runtime): us-east-1 primary. errors concentrated on the canary slice (10% traffic).

olivia (eng-platform): can we hit fast revert? we should avoid prolonged A/B noise.

raj (eng-ml): model itself not crashing; logs show deserialization timeouts when kv returns null for reshaped prompt tokens. Probably code path expecting prefix cached keys.

eva (devex): Can we safe-disable the affinity toggle in console? I can flip the UI guard but need the exact flag.

mike (eng-runtime): Flag is routing.session_affinity.enabled = true in rollout config. We did a progressive enable: 0 -> 10% -> 50%. Reverting to 0 should route everyone back to prior routing behavior. But note: session keyed caches might have stale entries.

sara (eng-sre): Plan proposal: 1) Pause canary traffic split to 0% for model-v3-small variant 2) TTL sweep for KV prefixes touched by canary 3) Revert affinity flag and restart a subset of router workers 4) Monitor 5xx/latency + top traces for 15m. If green, promote a safe rollout.

olivia (eng-platform): +1. Add a guard: if service error rate drops <1% for 15m then keep rollout paused; otherwise trigger automated rollback to model-v2 with full traffic. We need exact commands.

mike (eng-runtime): commands:
```
# fast revert traffic split
redwoodctl rollout update --route /generate --variant model-v3-small --traffic 0 --reason "fast-revert-1863456789"
# revert affinity flag
redwoodctl config set rollout.routing.session_affinity.enabled=false --target canary-1863
# restart router workers (graceful)
kubectl rollout restart deploy/router --namespace inference -l canary=1963
# kv ttl sweep (prefix)
redis-cli --scan --pattern "cache:prefix:model-v3-small:*" | xargs -n 100 redis-cli del
```

raj (eng-ml): caution: deleting KV keys will drop useful prefix caches and increase token cost briefly. Consider evicting only keys older than N seconds. We can use `redis-cli --raw` + ``--score`` checks if using sorted sets, otherwise store timestamps.

sara (eng-sre): Good point. We have a small helper script: `tools/kv-evict --prefix cache:prefix:model-v3-small --max-age 300` that soft-evicts. Use that first.

eva (devex): I'll open the console action: "Pause canary traffic" and annotate it with the rollback playbook link. Can someone paste a minimal checklist for the UI?

mike (eng-runtime): Checklist for console: 1) Pause traffic split for variant 2) Toggle session_affinity to previous value 3) Run soft-kv-evict 4) Restart 3 router pods gradually 5) Watch charts: 5xx, p50/p95 latency, kv-miss rate, token-per-request.

olivia (eng-platform): Add telemetry tasks: tag all incoming traces from the canary cohort (`cohort:canary-1863456789`) so we can filter traces post-ops. Also make sure rollout metrics include `model_variant` dimension in the next 24h.

raj (eng-ml): I pushed a quick patch to the canary to emit `kv_hit=false` when fallback happens. That will help isolate bad requests.

sara (eng-sre): I'll coordinate the rollback window: executing in 2 mins unless anyone objects. We need on-call from infra for the router restart (dennis?).

olivia (eng-platform): pinging @dennis (infra) but he's out; dennis left a runbook in #eng-infra last week. We can do a staggered restart without on-call if we keep to 1 pod at a time.

sara (eng-sre): executing now: running `tools/kv-evict --prefix cache:prefix:model-v3-small --max-age 300 --dry-run` first.

mike (eng-runtime): I'll stage the `redwoodctl rollout update` command but hold.

sara (eng-sre): dry-run shows ~9k keys aged >300s. switching to real run: `tools/kv-evict --prefix cache:prefix:model-v3-small --max-age 300`

[deploy-bot]: Start: rollout update triggered by sara at 1863456900

sara (eng-sre): executed traffic cut to 0% on canary. Confirming no immediate spike in 5xx.

mike (eng-runtime): flipping session_affinity to false now.

[deploy-bot]: Config change applied: rollout.routing.session_affinity.enabled=false at 1863456942

raj (eng-ml): KV eviction running. Partial CPU bump on redis, expect some increase in latency as caches warm.

eva (devex): console action recorded. I added links to the runbook and left a note for PMs.

sara (eng-sre): restarting router pods (one at a time) now. Pod 1 restarted, draining sessions.

mike (eng-runtime): seeing p95 dip a bit but 5xx holding steady. good sign.

olivia (eng-platform): telemetry tags in place. filtering traces for `cohort:canary-1863456789` shows most errors tied to `kv_hit=false` fallback path, good signal.

raj (eng-ml): suggests we follow up with a small A/B fix: make the model tolerant to missing prefix keys (fallback path) and add a soft delay rather than timeout. We'll prepare a patch and test in a dev canary.

sara (eng-sre): monitoring 10m window. If stable, we'll keep canary paused and schedule a controlled re-roll after fixes.

olivia (eng-platform): Agreed. Action items: mike/raj to patch fallback; eva to update rollout UX to show "soft-evict" option and warn about token cost; sara to write incident note and timeline; olivia will notify product and customers if SLA risk.

mike (eng-runtime): quick note: add a guard on the console that prevents enabling session_affinity for <5% initial traffic without a specific KV-compatibility flag. That should prevent this class of regressions.

eva (devex): I'll add UX copy and a tooltip: "Session affinity requires KV prefix compatibility; use only after validation."

olivia (eng-platform): Thanks all. I'll close the thread after 30m if metrics remain stable. :thumbsup:
